svg.text: How to Choose the Right Bedroom
A practical guide to lamp size, placement, light temperature and layering
We may earn a commission when you purchase through links on this page, at no additional cost to you.
Good bedroom lighting supports the way you use the room, from getting
dressed to settling down with a book. Begin with function, then consider
comfort and atmosphere. A thoughtful combination of light sources gives you
more flexibility than choosing one fixture to do everything.
Start With How You Use Your Bedroom
Before choosing fixtures, think about the activities that take place in the
room and where you need light for each one.
Identify the activities that need dedicated light before choosing individual fixtures.
Focused light for reading and other
Bedside lamps · Wall sconces · Reading lights
Choose a lamp in proportion to both the nightstand and the bed. Check the light from your usual seated
Keep reading light and controls within comfortable reach. Consider whether a
table lamp or wall sconce best suits the space.
Use general lighting to help you see and move around the room. Consider how
it works alongside your other light sources.
A secondary light can make this area more useful while adding another layer
Position focused light where you sit, with attention to glare and the
Often chosen for a relaxed atmosphere. Consider how the light feels
alongside your wall colors and textiles.
Can feel crisper. Color temperature describes the appearance of light; it
does not tell you how bright a bulb is.
Choose comfortable illumination for relaxing, with enough focused light for

Match Lighting to Your Design Style
A single ceiling fixture may not support every activity. Plan a combination
CHOOSING A LAMP THAT IS TOO LARGE
Consider the shade as well as the base. Leave enough space for the everyday
objects you keep beside the bed.
Decorative lighting may not direct enough light onto a page. Consider a
dedicated task light where it is useful.
Check that switches are easy to reach from the places where you actually use
A compact design can leave more room for bedside essentials. Compare its
full dimensions with the space you measured.
An adjustable design can help position light where you read. Consider the
location of both the switch and the beam.
A simple sculptural form can complement a contemporary room. Balance the
decorative shape with the lighting function you need.
